rationale: The child is a brief ceremonial welcome to a visiting foreign president, centered on an imminent meeting, lunch, treaty signing, and cordial wishes for the visit. C09 is the closest in diplomatic tone and expression of friendship, while C11 is correspondence with a foreign head of government and C23 uses personal appreciation and good wishes in a diplomatic context. However, their similarities are limited to routine diplomatic-letter conventions and generic cordial language. None contains the child's distinctive welcome-and-itinerary structure or plausibly supplied a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Permit me again to extend to you a most cordial welcome
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to take this opportunity to express to you again the friendship and good will
shared_material.explanation: C09 shares a courteous diplomatic expression addressed to a foreign representative, but the phrasing and function are generic and do not establish templating.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to express the hope that this visit in the United States will be both pleasant and profitable
shared_material.explanation: C11 shares only a conventional cordial closing in correspondence with a foreign leader.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It always gives me the greatest pleasure to welcome you to Washington
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I extend also my very best wishes in connection with the important new responsibilities you are about to assume
shared_material.explanation: C23 similarly offers personal good wishes to a diplomat, but it is an appointment letter with no parallel welcome, visit, or meeting sequence.
